fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the specific atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating and 550 °C annealing intervention with an unspecified surface-enrichment treatment.
It introduces combined irradiation exposure and a Ni-rich self-healing oxide as governing features, neither of which is part of the target study or established by the cited evidence.
The proposed environments do not reproduce the target 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemistry or 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion conditions.
The cited studies do not directly demonstrate Cr/Ni passive-film self-repair under simultaneous corrosion and irradiation.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion-resistant steels and proposes a testable passive-film mechanism, but it does not reconstruct the target material, processing route, or exposure conditions. Its only substantial mechanistic overlap is the general role of chromium-bearing passive oxides and the prediction of increased polarization resistance and reduced corrosion current. It omits the AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating, APS parameters, 550 °C optimum anneal, refined BCC/FCC microstructure, Al-rich oxides, micropore-mediated salt ingress, high-temperature cyclic testing, and mass-gain outcomes. The controlled-damage experiment, in situ film analysis, control group, and explicit falsification rule provide useful discrimination, although the treatment and operational boundaries remain vague. Evidence E3 supports compact passive films and EIS assessment, but E1 concerns solute-dislocation interactions, E2 irradiation-defect behavior, and E4 atomistic chemical ordering; collectively they do not validate Ni-rich self-healing passivation under coupled irradiation and corrosion. Thus the proposal is a scientifically plausible alternative rather than a reconstruction of the hidden study.
